title: A shocking 92 percent of US adults are not going to the doctor because it’s too expensive
excerpt: The decision to delay medical care involves multiple factors, including gender - women are more likely to put off care than men
content_html:
An overwhelming number of Americans are delaying medical care because of fears they can’t afford it, a new study has found.

Some 92 percent have delayed or abandoned medical care because of costs, according to a survey of 1,507 U.S.adults by financial services firm JG Wentworth.

Those aged 18 to 28 are the most likely to delay or avoid care because of cost (94.2 percent), followed by those aged 29 to 44.

“The findings highlight a growing gap between having health insurance and feeling financially protected, with medical costs forcing many Americans to delay treatment, cut essential spending and take on debt,” the study said.

The decision to delay medical care involves multiple issues, including gender - women are more likely to put off care than men. Other factors include age and whether or not someone has health insurance.

A doctor’s office visit for those without insurance costs an average of $171 across major U.S. cities, according to a February 2026 analysis by healthcare provider marketplace Zocdoc.

High prices at the doctor’s office, urgent care, emergency room and more have led to 85 percent of Americans having medical debt.

Collectively, American consumers have $220 billion in medical debt, according to a February poll from KFF - that’s around $958.61 per adult with medical debt.

There are a wide range of consequences for delaying doctor’s visits, a May 2025 survey from KFF found. Nearly one in five adults said their health got worse because they skipped a doctor’s visit. That problem is more acute for those 64 and younger - 42 percent say their health got worse after putting off a medical visit.

The problem bleeds over into prescription drug costs, too, an April KFF study discovered. Some 31 percent of adults say they’ve opted for over-the-counter medication instead of prescription drugs because of costs. Another 19 percent say they skip prescription doses or cut pills in half to make their medication last.

Healthcare costs aren’t expected to go down through 2027, a June study from financial firm PwC found.

“Health plans are projecting the highest medical cost trend in nearly two decades, with commercial healthcare cost trend expected to rise to 9 [percent] in 2027,” the study said.

Factors such as AI-enabled revenue optimization tools and more use of behavioral health benefits will influence the increase, PwC noted.

The Trump administration has proposed several strategies for lower healthcare costs with “The Great Healthcare Plan,” which, among other things, calls for lowering what Americans pay for medication by getting most-favored-nation pricing from countries that send medication to the U.S.

The U.S. secured most-favored-nation pricing with 16 pharmaceutical companies. Yet 953 of the 971 drugs available through most-favored status went up in price in January 2026, according to an analysis from data analytics site 46brooklyn.

That number of price hikes is the second-highest in the past five years. Only January 2023 had a higher number of price increases - 960.

Beyond healthcare, consumers are navigating an inflation rate that’s risen quickly since February thanks to rocketing energy costs resulting from President Donald Trump’s war with Iran.

Since dropping to 2.4 percent in February, inflation rose to 3.3 percent in March, 4.2 percent in May and fell to 3.5 percent in June.

Consumer confidence plummeted to a record low in May, signaling that people felt unprecedented pessimism about the state of the economy and high inflation rates.

content_html_zh:
一项新的研究发现，绝大多数美国人因为担心负担不起而推迟医疗服务。

金融服务公司 JG Wentworth 对 1,507 名美国成年人进行的一项调查显示，约 92% 的人因费用问题而推迟或放弃医疗护理。

18 至 28 岁的人群最有可能因费用而推迟或避免护理（94.2%），其次是 29 至 44 岁的人群。

该研究称：“调查结果突显了拥有健康保险和感到经济受到保护之间的差距越来越大，医疗费用迫使许多美国人推迟治疗、削减基本支出并承担债务。”

推迟医疗护理的决定涉及多个问题，其中包括性别——女性比男性更有可能推迟医疗护理。 其他因素包括年龄以及某人是否有健康保险。

根据医疗保健提供商市场 Zocdoc 2026 年 2 月的分析，在美国主要城市，没有保险的人看医生的平均费用为 171 美元。

医生办公室、紧急护理、急诊室等的高昂价格导致 85% 的美国人背负着医疗债务。

根据 KFF 2 月份的一项民意调查，美国消费者总共背负着 2200 亿美元的医疗债务，即每个成年人背负的医疗债务约为 958.61 美元。

KFF 2025 年 5 月的一项调查发现，延迟就诊会产生多种后果。 近五分之一的成年人表示，由于没有去看医生，他们的健康状况变得更糟。 对于 64 岁及以下的人来说，这个问题更为严重——42% 的人表示，推迟就诊后，他们的健康状况变得更糟。

KFF 4 月份的一项研究发现，这个问题也影响到了处方药的成本。 约 31% 的成年人表示，由于成本原因，他们选择了非处方药而不是处方药。 另外 19% 的人表示，他们会跳过处方剂量或将药片减半，以保证药物持续有效。

金融公司普华永道 (PwC) 6 月份的一项研究发现，预计到 2027 年，医疗保健成本不会下降。

研究称：“健康计划预计医疗成本将出现近二十年来最高的趋势，商业医疗成本趋势预计将在 2027 年升至 9%。”

普华永道指出，人工智能支持的收入优化工具和更多地使用行为健康福利等因素将影响这一增长。

特朗普政府通过“伟大的医疗保健计划”提出了几项降低医疗保健成本的策略，其中包括呼吁通过从向美国运送药品的国家获得最惠国定价来降低美国人的药品支付费用。

美国与16家制药公司获得最惠国定价。 然而，根据数据分析网站 46brooklyn 的分析，2026 年 1 月，971 种可享受最优惠待遇的药物中有 953 种价格上涨。

这一涨价次数是过去五年来第二高的。 仅 2023 年 1 月的涨价次数就更多 - 960 次。

除了医疗保健之外，由于唐纳德·特朗普总统与伊朗的战争导致能源成本飙升，消费者还面临着自二月份以来迅速上升的通货膨胀率。

自2月份降至2.4%以来，3月份通胀率升至3.3%，5月份升至4.2%，6月份降至3.5%。

5月份消费者信心跌至历史新低，表明人们对经济状况和高通胀率感到前所未有的悲观情绪。
